title: Human subthalamic nucleus microelectrode recordings during an interrupted reach task (London et al., 2021)
description: Intraoperative microelectrode recordings from the subthalamic nucleus of Parkinson's disease patients undergoing deep brain stimulation surgery. Patients performed an extended touchscreen reaching task in which the target sometimes changed mid-movement (interrupted reach). The release contains wideband raw microelectrode and macro-contact signals from 8 subjects (16 task blocks, about 2.57 h), with task events and source behavioural and spike-sorted data.
methods_description: Patients were off anti-Parkinsonian medication. One or two tungsten Neuroprobe Sonus microelectrodes (1 MOhm, Alpha Omega), 2 mm apart on a single microdrive, were referenced to the outer cannula. Raw signals were sampled at 44 kHz (22 kHz for one subject), exported from Alpha Omega, scaled to µV and written as BrainVision float32, with port/TTL events in events.tsv.
